clue.text: Disruptively call greedy VIP a "baronet with debts"

definitions.note: a fictional title-holder drowning in money troubles

indicators.note: acting disruptively throws things into disorder, so the letters of the three words before it are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone rudely calls a grasping celebrity an indebted baronet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Disruptively' rearranges CALL GREEDY VIP; the 'a' and the quotation marks only join the clue together.
explanation.definitionFit: In Wilkie Collins's The Woman in White, Sir Percival Glyde is a baronet whose crushing debts drive the plot.

clue.text: King George is laughing after introduction to noble American birds, in a poem

annotationWithheld.why: King George is laughing after introduction to noble American birds, in a poem (6,8): PURPLE GRACKLES is Amy Lowell's poem, but 'King George is laughing' gives GR + CACKLES, one C too many for GRACKLES, and 'introduction to noble' does not plainly give PURPLE; no clean parse found
annotationWithheld.clue: King George is laughing after introduction to noble American birds, in a poem

clue.text: Ron received information about Troy and he discovered Ray

parts.note: t is the abbreviation for troy, the weight system for precious metals
gen is British slang for information that has been passed on

explanation.surface: A man named Ron gets the facts about Troy, and someone else discovered a ray.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' is a link meaning 'on the subject of'. 'Ray' is capitalised to pass for a man's name; the ray meant is the X-ray.
explanation.definitionFit: Wilhelm Röntgen, the German physicist, discovered X-rays in 1895, and they are still called Röntgen rays.

clue.text: Quick route to wealth is sought in this 1960s comic novel

definitions.text: Quick route to wealth is sought in this 1960s comic novel

parts.words: Quick route to wealth is sought in this 1960s comic novel
parts.note: the novel's title is the very cry of someone wanting riches without delay

explanation.walkthrough: Kingsley Amis's 1968 comic novel follows a TV presenter chasing a rich heiress; its title voices impatience for money.
explanation.definitionFit: The title names Kingsley Amis's 1968 comic novel about a television personality hungry for instant riches.

clue.text: European route — entirely European — leading to Spain

parts.note: all can mean wholly or completely, as in 'all wrong'
E is the international vehicle registration letter for Spain (España)

explanation.surface: A road across the continent, wholly within Europe, ends up in Spain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leading to' just joins the pieces. An allée is a French tree-lined walk, so a European route.
explanation.definitionFit: An allée is a formal avenue or path, usually lined with trees, in French gardens and towns.

clue.text: Good old London dandy's penniless, or a dealer in high-end goods?

annotationWithheld.why: Good old London dandy's penniless, or a dealer in high-end goods? (9): GOLDSMITH fits the second definition and Oliver Goldsmith, the penniless and dandyish London writer, but no wordplay found giving SMITH from 'London dandy's penniless'
annotationWithheld.clue: Good old London dandy's penniless, or a dealer in high-end goods?

clue.text: Immature people seeing nothing in actress Claire's comeback

indicators.note: a comeback is a return, so the letters are read in the opposite direction
the word in places one piece inside the actress's surname

parts.note: Claire Foy is the English actress who played the Queen in The Crown
O is the zero shape, so nothing gives O

explanation.surface: Young people notice nothing in an actress's return to the screen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts O inside FOY to make FOOY, and 'comeback' turns that around. Yoof is British slang, mimicking a London accent, for young people.
explanation.definitionFit: Yoof is jokey British slang for youth, young people seen as a group with their own culture.

clue.text: One visiting key — dangerous island

parts.note: E is one of the musical keys

indicators.note: a visitor goes into a place, so one piece is put inside another

parts.note: risky means dangerous
A means one, as in 'a pound'

explanation.surface: A traveller calls at a Florida key, and it proves a hazardous island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'key' looks like a Florida Key; it is the musical key E. 'visiting' puts A inside RISKY.
explanation.definitionFit: Eriskay is a small island in the Outer Hebrides, off the west coast of Scotland.

clue.text: Saint and symbol of England captivating Victorian vicar's son from Yorkshire

indicators.note: to captivate is to hold captive, so the two outer pieces enclose another

parts.note: Saint George is the patron saint of England
the red rose is the national flower and emblem of England
Victorian can mean prudish and straitlaced, which is prim

explanation.surface: A saint and the national flower enchant the vicar's boy from Yorkshire.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Victorian' looks like a date for the vicar's son; it means prudish. 'captivating' has the saint and the flower close around the prudish word, as one pair.
explanation.definitionFit: In Goldsmith's novel The Vicar of Wakefield, set in Yorkshire, George is the eldest son of the vicar, Dr Primrose.

clue.text: Scottish song writer's purpose in an instruction to slow down

indicators.note: the word in puts one piece inside the musical direction

parts.note: rall. is the short form of rallentando, the musical direction to slow down gradually
an end is an aim or purpose, as in 'to that end'

explanation.surface: A Scots songwriter's aim is set out in a direction to take the tempo down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'writer's' is 'writer is'. RALL is the score's abbreviation for rallentando.
explanation.definitionFit: Robert Rendall was an Orkney poet who wrote verse in Scots, so a Scottish writer of lyric poems.

clue.text: Pope's kind of Latin verse

definitions.meaning: belonging to a pope called Leo
medieval Latin verse whose lines rhyme in the middle and at the end

explanation.walkthrough: 'Pope' tempts you toward Alexander Pope the poet; here it is any pope named Leo.
explanation.definitionFit: Named after Pope Leo, the word describes his things and also a medieval verse form with internal rhyme.

clue.text: Illuminate very old Irish poetry

parts.note: to light something is to illuminate it
Erse is an old name for the Gaelic languages of Ireland and Scotland

explanation.surface: A scholar sheds light on ancient Irish verse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Illuminate' seems the definition but is the first piece; 'very old Irish' splits into V and ERSE.
explanation.definitionFit: Light verse is humorous or playful poetry, such as limericks and comic rhymes.

clue.text: Kromesky really includes this Nordic foodstuff

indicators.note: the phrase before it contains the answer's letters running across its two words

explanation.surface: A Russian-style croquette apparently contains a Scandinavian dairy product.
explanation.walkthrough: A kromesky is a fried croquette of meat or fish wrapped in bacon.
explanation.definitionFit: Skyr is a thick Icelandic cultured dairy product, much like strained yogurt.

clue.text: Catastrophic defeat reportedly is a common trope in dramatic literature

parts.note: tragic means disastrous or catastrophic

indicators.note: reportedly means as people say it, so a word is replaced by one sounding the same

parts.note: to floor an opponent is to knock them down and so defeat them

explanation.surface: A crushing defeat, so people say, is a familiar device in plays.
explanation.walkthrough: FLOOR said in a non-rhotic British accent sounds like FLAW. 'is a' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Aristotle's hamartia, the hero's fatal weakness that brings his fall, is the staple of tragic drama.

clue.text: Taking ecstasy makes a cultured chap into a vagabond

indicators.note: the chap takes something in, so one piece goes inside another

parts.note: gent, short for gentleman, a refined and civilised man
E is the street abbreviation for the drug ecstasy

explanation.surface: A gentleman on drugs is transformed into a tramp.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Taking' puts E inside GENT. The answer is Jean Genet, the French writer who lived as a thief and vagrant before he wrote.
explanation.definitionFit: Jean Genet spent his youth as a petty thief and wanderer across Europe, which his Thief's Journal recounts.

clue.text: Myth I concocted with Lear's poetic style in the Lady of Shallot

definitions.text: poetic style in the Lady of Shallot

indicators.note: something concocted is made up from mixed ingredients, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: a possessive adds no letter; the name is used as written

explanation.surface: A made-up myth plus Edward Lear's nonsense manner describes Tennyson's famous poem.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lear's poetic style' is a false trail: Lear is just fodder. 'Shallot' is a punning misspelling of Tennyson's Shalott.
explanation.definitionFit: Tennyson's poem uses stanzas where a short refrain line closes each group of rhyming lines, the tail-rhyme pattern.

clue.text: Head avatar one's missing badly in oriental form of religion

indicators.note: done badly, the letters come out in a muddled order

parts.note: a is one, as in 'a dozen'; the 's here stands for is

explanation.surface: A leading god incarnate has gone astray in an Eastern faith.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one's missing' says to drop one A from the first two words before 'badly' rearranges what remains.
explanation.definitionFit: Theravada is the oldest surviving school of Buddhism, followed in Sri Lanka and South-East Asia.

clue.text: This love goddess could make hearts hot

indicators.note: the words could be made into something else, so their letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A goddess of love can set hearts ablaze.
explanation.walkthrough: 'could make' rearranges HEARTS HOT.
explanation.definitionFit: Ashtoreth is the Hebrew Bible's name for Astarte, the Phoenician goddess of fertility and sexual love.

clue.text: Greek philosopher dispensed with one struggling with apathy

indicators.note: the letters struggle and twist about, so they are rearranged

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A thinker is cast aside by someone fighting against indifference.
explanation.walkthrough: Hypatia of Alexandria was murdered by a mob in 415, so 'dispensed with' belongs to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Hypatia, a Neoplatonist mathematician and teacher in Alexandria, was killed by a Christian mob in AD 415.

clue.text: Colt maybe, or a more dangerous animal in America

definitions.text: a more dangerous animal in America

parts.note: a Colt revolver is an example of a gat, old American slang for a gun
taken as written

explanation.surface: A young horse, or perhaps something fiercer, roams America.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Colt' looks like a young horse beside 'animal'; it is the gun. A gator is an American alligator.
explanation.definitionFit: Gator, short for alligator, is the everyday American name for the big reptile, far deadlier than a colt.

clue.text: Playwright's letter about Royal Enclosure

indicators.note: about here means around, so one piece goes round the others

parts.note: tee is the spelt-out name of the letter T
R is the abbreviation for royal, as in RN
enc. is the abbreviation for enclosure at the foot of a letter

explanation.surface: A dramatist writes to the Royal Enclosure at Ascot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Royal Enclosure' is the members' area at Ascot races, a false picture; split, the two words give abbreviations that 'about' puts inside the spelt-out letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Terence was the Roman comic playwright of the second century BC.

clue.text: Reserved sort of man

definitions.meaning: set aside or held back for someone, as in 'retained'
a man supported financially by a lover

explanation.definitionFit: Things reserved are held back for later; and a man financially maintained by a lover is so described.

clue.text: Scruffy 18th-century London philanthropist's maid, in fiction

parts.note: tatty means shabby or scruffy
Thomas Coram founded the Foundling Hospital in London in 1739

explanation.surface: A shabby charity founder's servant appears in a story.
explanation.walkthrough: The orphan was named after Thomas Coram's Foundling Hospital, where she was raised.
explanation.definitionFit: In Dickens's Little Dorrit, Harriet Beadle, called Tattycoram, is the maid of the Meagles family.

clue.text: Ugly large LOTR character

parts.note: a hulking, brutish monster from Tolkien's books, one of a kind that turns to stone in daylight

explanation.definitionFit: Tolkien's trolls in The Lord of the Rings are huge, ugly, dim-witted creatures.

clue.text: Overseas airline's American replaced by United for one month

indicators.note: one letter of the airline is swapped out and another put in its place

parts.note: El Al is Israel's national airline
U is an abbreviation for United, as in Manchester Utd or USA

explanation.surface: A foreign carrier swaps its American partner for United for a month.
explanation.walkthrough: 'replaced by' changes the second A of ELAL into a U.
explanation.definitionFit: Elul is the sixth month of the Jewish civil year, falling in August and September.

clue.text: Is French jazz singer a former Bentley fan?

parts.note: est is French for is
Ella Fitzgerald, the great American jazz singer

explanation.surface: A French singer is asked whether she once loved a vintage car.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bentley' is not the car: it is Bentley Drummle of Great Expectations, whom Estella marries and later is free of.
explanation.definitionFit: In Dickens's Great Expectations, Estella chooses and marries the brutish Bentley Drummle, who later dies.

clue.text: Lover of Rosalind, or Norris?

parts.note: taken as written
Lando Norris is the British Formula One driver

explanation.surface: Who loved Rosalind: this man, or perhaps someone called Norris?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Norris' looks like a rival suitor; it gives the racing driver's first name, Lando.
explanation.definitionFit: In Shakespeare's As You Like It, Orlando falls in love with Rosalind and pins verses to trees in the Forest of Arden.

clue.text: Supernatural novel in which everyone's greeting a famous golfer

parts.note: all means everyone; the 's stands for is and adds no letter
hallow is an old variant of halloo, a shout of greeting
Seve Ballesteros, the Spanish golf champion

explanation.surface: A ghost story in which the whole crowd hails a celebrated golfer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'everyone's' is 'everyone is'. Charles Williams's 1945 novel is set among the dead in London.
explanation.definitionFit: Charles Williams, an Inkling, wrote this 1945 supernatural novel about a dead woman's spirit wandering London.
